abstract: Human pluripotent stem cell-derived heart organoids have emerged as powerful models of human cardiac development, disease, and therapeutic responses. Here, we present the first integrated single-cell transcriptomic atlas of human cardiac organoids, combining 16 datasets generated across diverse differentiation strategies into a unified reference framework. The atlas resolves protocol-dependent effects on lineage composition, developmental fidelity, and cellular maturation, enabling direct comparison of cardiac organoid systems across the field. Mapping to fetal and adult heart references demonstrates that organoid-derived populations faithfully recapitulate early first-trimester developmental states, with maturation representing the major remaining bottleneck. The analysis identifies reproducible generation of epicardial and coronary vascular lineages, reveals distinct trade-offs between cellular diversity and maturation across protocols, and benchmarks organoids against complementary 3D cardiac models and newly generated datasets. Finally, drug-target analyses expose signaling pathways that remain insufficiently represented in vitro. This community resource provides a standardized framework for evaluating, comparing, and improving human cardiac differentiation models.
